I did not run Lean. Whether `simp` rewrites `Symmetrify.of.obj x` through Mathlib's `Symmetrify.of_obj` (stated as `of.obj = id`) relies on my understanding of how simp handles over-applied rewrite rules. findings.problem: The docstring says rewriting `Symmetrify.of.obj x` to `x` is deliberately kept out of the simp set. But Mathlib's `Symmetrify.of` is declared `@[simps]` with `obj := id`, which generates the simp lemma `Quiver.Symmetrify.of_obj`. As I read it, plain `simp` already erases `Symmetrify.of.obj x` (to `id x`, then `x`). So the design rationale is not true of the actual simp set, and `symmetrify_of_obj` is a non-simp duplicate of a simp lemma. The rest of the file follows from this. `card_symmetrify_hom` states its left-hand side with `Symmetrify.of.obj i ⟶ Symmetrify.of.obj j`, which simp would rewrite to `i ⟶ j` before the lemma could match. Callers therefore need `rw`, and `A2/Basic.lean` uses `simp only [symmetrify_of_obj]`.
findings.proposed_change: Decide the normal form explicitly. One option is to drop `symmetrify_of_obj` and use the existing `Symmetrify.of_obj` together with `id_eq`. Another is to keep it under a name that does not suggest it is the only rewrite, and replace the 'Deliberately not a simp lemma' sentence with an accurate statement that Mathlib's `Symmetrify.of_obj` is simp. If the aim is a normal form that keeps `Symmetrify.of`, the right fix is a local `simp [-Symmetrify.of_obj]` in the callers. Separately, restate `card_symmetrify_hom` in the simp-normal form `Fintype.card (x ⟶ y)` for `x y : Symmetrify Q`, so that it can be used by `simp`. Alternatively, record that it is `rw`-only.
findings.benefit: The docstring would match the real simp behaviour, so readers are not misled about whether `simp` erases `Symmetrify.of`. Having one canonical rewrite for `of.obj x` also removes a duplicate rule. The card lemma would then be usable from simp calls, with no need for `rw` or an explicit `simp only [symmetrify_of_obj]`.
